idea: Classic Tory grandee, late fifties: the deep, drawling, plummy RP of a public-school old boy, indignant rather than shouting. The class gap from the crew comes from the vowels and the entitlement, and it is the most recognisable British TV 'posh minister'.
tone: A man in his late fifties with a deep, rich, plummy upper-class English accent, the clipped Received Pronunciation of Eton and Oxford. A Conservative cabinet minister on his mobile in the back of a chauffeured car, outraged and put upon, speaking down to a junior aide. Long drawled vowels, crisp consonants, a pained sigh before the line, then rising indignation that peaks on the last word. Spoken alone, dry and close, voice only, like a British television drama.
